Off-peak simple rules for tag checks for new staff
This page teaches a habit of care

This page matters because the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps travel smooth for passengers and safe for animals, and small tag errors can delay boarding, confuse crews, or create stress for the pet. New staff must learn to read each label with steady attention and treat every record as live until the last check is complete. Work in plain steps. Start with the animal tag, then the carrier tag, then the passenger record, and then compare the details again before any handoff. If anything looks blurred, torn, or out of place, stop and bring in the senior coordinator at once.

Use the desk notes to confirm that the pet and the traveler match across all forms. Check the name spelling, the route, the crate type, and any care note that affects handling. If a traveler arrives worried, keep the tone calm and brief. Say what you are checking, do not guess, and do not move on until the records agree. A pet may seem settled, but do not rely on appearance alone; the tags and the file must support each other. If two documents conflict, set the case aside and report it without delay.

Crews depend on clean handovers. Place the approved tag where it can be seen, keep the strap secure, and make sure old labels are removed when they no longer apply. Never leave a loose tag inside the carrier area. If a tag is missing, damaged, or wet, replace it through the desk process and record the change right away. Keep your notes simple and exact. Use the same terms every time so the next staff member can follow the trace without confusion. A clear note can prevent a rushed mistake at the gate.

When you handle a case from start to finish, remember that the goal is not speed alone. It is safe passage, calm contact, and a record that can be trusted by the next shift. Keep your eyes on the tags, your hands steady, and your report complete. What to remember is that careful tag checks protect every traveler and every animal.
